text:
maria.sales: Hey team — acme sec asked detailed followups on BYOK/HSM for the POC. Can we confirm what we can tell them for the SIG/CAIQ responses?

alex.lewis: Short version: we support customer-managed keys via BYOK, can integrate with AWS KMS/GCP KMS or bring-your-own HSM (PKCS#11). For POC we can accept temporary keys or a customer-supplied KMS key policy.

jordan.security: For SIG/CAIQ, they usually want exact control plane vs data plane separation, key custody, attestations, and rotation cadence. Suggested answer: "Customer-managed keys (BYOK) supported; HSM-backed keys meet FIPS 140-2/140-3 L2/L3 as provided by the customer's HSM vendor; Redwood does not retain plaintext master keys."

alex.lewis: Addendum: clarify we can do two modes for POC: 1) customer KMS with grant to Redwood service account (no key material leaves customer KMS) or 2) customer exports a wrapped key to Redwood under a temporary envelope key for the POC (we recommend mode 1).

maria.sales: Customer asked about rotation windows — they want an explicit policy we can paste in the SIG matrix.

jordan.security: Paste-able policy text: "Data encryption keys (DEKs) are rotated monthly; Key encrypting keys (KEKs)/master keys are rotated at least annually or when cryptographic compromise is suspected. For BYOK, rotation is managed by the customer’s KMS; Redwood supports re-wrapping and key rollover with zero-downtime key rotation procedures."

eng-crypto-bot: FYI, from our docs: ```yaml
# example: aws-kms grant workflow (POC)
redwood:
  kms_integration: aws-kms
  external_key_arn: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01
  grant_principal: redwood-inference-poc-role
  key_policy_notes: "Grant encrypt/decrypt only; do not grant DescribeKey to third parties"
```

alex.lewis: For HSM/BYOK technical notes: we support PKCS#11 & KMIP gateways for on-prem HSMs. We can accept HSM attestation docs and the vendor cert chain. For SOC2/SIG evidence, provide HSM FIPS cert, attestation report, and customer KMS audit logs.

priya.custsuccess: Customer also wants to know if we cache plaintext keys in memory during inference and how that's protected. Can we give a short, non-legal answer for the presales deck?

jordan.security: Use this short blurb: "Redwood only decrypts wrapped keys within a hardened key manager boundary; unwrapped DEKs exist in memory only inside a secure enclave process and are purged immediately after use. Access to key material is limited to the runtime components required for inference and is logged/monitored."

maria.sales: Perfect. Can we also give the POC steps for their security team to sign off?

alex.lewis: POC checklist (short): 1) Share customer KMS ARN or HSM endpoint + attestation docs. 2) Setup grant/role for Redwood POC IAM principal. 3) Test encrypt/decrypt flow with a test key/credentials. 4) Run sample inference workload while capturing CloudTrail/KMS logs. 5) Validate rotation and key rollover (we provide scripts). 6) Collect logs/attestation for SIG response.

priya.custsuccess: I'll schedule the kickoff at 10am PT Tue. Maria — can you send the customer-facing text bundle (SIG answers + policy + checklist)?

maria.sales: On it. I'll compile a single ZIP with the SIG answers, the rotation policy text, the example AWS snippet, and the checklist. Will ping when uploaded. :thumbsup:

alex.lewis: If anyone needs more formalized language for CAIQ questions, I can draft exact Q/A mappings for the checklist items (eg. SC-13, CR-3).

jordan.security: +1, please include references to our SOC2 and the recommendation to include HSM attestation artifacts in the vendor package.

maria.sales: Thanks everyone — will update thread when bundle is ready.
